full_judgment: 17. By a careful consideration of all the above facts and circumstances and the position of the case, I find that the impugned judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge is not based on correct evaluation of the facts and materials of the case nor proper appreciation of the evidence on record. I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal. I, therefore, find that the learned Subordinate judge has committed an error resulting in an error of law in his decision which has occasioned a failure of justice to the defendant-petitioner. The impugned judgment, in my opinion, suffers from infirmity. Hence it calls for interference by this court.
